title: Adaptive fragment coalescer and proactive eviction policy for paged KV cache
creator: Asha Narayanan
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements an adaptive fragment coalescer plus a proactive eviction prioritizer for our paged KV cache used by paged-attention models. The goal is to reduce fragmentation-induced memory amplification, reduce decode tail-latency variance, and avoid expensive on-demand prefill stalls during inference surges.

Motivation & background:
- Current paged KV allocation is conservative and leaves small free fragments scattered across slabs when sessions with variable sequence lengths are interleaved. That increases page table size, increases scatter-gather during prefill, and forces more frequent page reads from remote storage on cold-paths.
- Previous work (ENG-31807, ENG-27340) improved prefill scheduling and LRU windows but left mid-life fragmentation unaddressed; ops saw a 7-12% CPU overhead for mixed short/long workloads.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Fragment coalescer: Background worker that opportunistically merges adjacent free fragments within a slab when coalescing cost estimate < amortized decode cost saved. Uses lightweight per-slab bitmaps and a small budgeted window to avoid CPU spikes. Coalescer runs at configurable low priority and is throttled based on current SLO headroom.
2) Proactive eviction prioritizer: Eviction policy that scores candidates not just by recency but by fragmentation impact, expected reuse probability (from session histograms), and prefill cost if evicted (estimated bytes to re-prefill). The scoring formula is tunable and includes a multiplier for critical customers / dedicated pools.
3) Prefill-aware admission: When admitting a large prefill, the allocator will attempt inlined coalescing on target slab candidates to make room rather than immediately falling back to remote page fetch. If inlined coalescing would exceed a latency budget, we fallback to best-effort partial prefill + streaming decode.
4) Metrics and guards: New metrics: fragment_count_by_slab, coalesce_ops/sec, avg_fragment_size_hist, eviction_score_distribution, prefill_stall_rate. Circuit breaker that pauses coalescer if CPU > threshold or if observed decode SLO breaches.

Trade-offs considered:
- CPU vs memory fragmentation: Aggressive coalescing reduces fragmentation but costs CPU; we bias towards low-priority background windows and tie activity to SLO slack.
- Latency spikes: Inline coalescing during admission can spike a request; we only allow this when the request is not latency-critical or when the admission batch is predicted to reduce downstream prefill cost.
- Complexity of reuse prediction: We use a simple exponential moving average of reuse per session+model to avoid high-cardinality ML models in the runtime. This keeps memory and CPU footprint predictable.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (spike + prototype): Implement slab bitmap and a unit-tested coalescer that merges adjacent free-run ranges. Add config knobs and a canary runtime flag. (Deliverable: proto coalescer, unit tests, microbench harness)
Phase 2 (integration): Wire coalescer into allocator, add eviction scoring hook, implement basic reuse EMA, and expose metrics. Run offline sims on production traces for 14 days to tune scoring parameters. (Deliverable: feature flag gated rollout, bench reports)
Phase 3 (canary + rollout): Enable in canary cluster for mixed short/long workload tenants; collect metrics, validate SLO impact, iterate on throttling. (Deliverable: canary dashboard, PRs, rollback plan)

Acceptance criteria:
- 10-25% reduction in fragment_count_by_slab for mixed workloads in canary compared to baseline.
- No >5% increase in 95th percentile decode CPU time on canary tenants.
- Prefill_stall_rate drops by at least 20% for tenants with interleaved session lengths.
- Expose tunables and circuit breaker that allow ops to safely disable coalescer at runtime.

Observability & tests:
- Unit tests for bitmap coalescing edge cases (wrap, single-run, multiple adjacent runs).
- Integration tests for eviction scoring stability under synthetic traffic (short-only, long-only, mixed).
- Offline trace replay harness: run historical traces from 2025-Q4 production to compute expected prefill bytes and simulated cost if eviction happens.
- Dashboards: slab-level fragment heatmap, eviction-score ladder, canary vs baseline latency/cost.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Coalescer CPU could compete with decode and increase tail latency. Mitigation: SLO-aware throttling and CPU budget, and an immediate disable when SLO breaches are observed.
- Risk: Scoring misclassifies long-lived small fragments as evictable. Mitigation: EMA tuned to favor longer reuse and fallback rule to never evict pinned pages (few hot keys).

Links & artifacts:
- Spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/ENG-40321+coalescer+spike
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2048
- Trace replay harness: gs://redwood-prod-traces/2025-q4/replay-set-3

Next steps (short term):
- Complete unit tests for coalescer (owner: Miguel), finalize scoring formula draft (owner: Asha), schedule offline 14-day replay (owner: SRE).
- Add feature flag gating and a follow-up ENGRollout doc describing canary selection criteria.

2026-02-28 | Lena Becker (SRE): Ran 7-day replay; prefill_stall_rate decreased 22% for mixed workloads. Observed one canary tenant with decode 95p +7% during heavy coalescing periods; added circuit breaker threshold proposal.
